pain_map.pain: The within-target skeptic is a LAPSED buyer whose real blocker is behavioral, not product: the ad wins credibility on purity but has no answer for 'I'm not training,' so every unit of earned trust dies at consideration because the buyer projects a repeat of the stale-tub regret. The creative persuades the head of a person whose hand won't move.
pain_map.prevalence: near-universal among within-target skeptic_lapsed_protein across all contexts

evidence_quotes.quote: I still don't actually have a workout routine, so spending money on protein powder again feels like setting up the exact same situation where a bag just sits on my shelf going stale.
spending ₹3,500 or whatever this costs on something that requires the thing I'm not doing is just the same mistake at a higher price point.
buying this is just spending ₹2,500-odd on powder that sits on my shelf doing nothing — same movie, different packaging.

pain_map.pain: The QR-to-lab-reports mechanic is the single strongest trust asset the ad owns, but it terminates as an off-ad deferral rather than an on-surface payoff: within-target and ambiguous buyers reach 'I'd scan/check' and defer to a search that mostly never converts, so the ad's best proof point leaks interest between comprehension and consideration instead of closing it.
pain_map.prevalence: widespread across skeptic (within) and enthusiast (ambiguous), all research/browse contexts

evidence_quotes.quote: The test reports claim is the first specific, verifiable thing I've seen in this category, so I'd scan that QR code before anything else — not to buy, just to check if the number actually holds up.
I'd scan that QR code to check the actual lab reports before anything else, because that's the one claim here I can actually verify.
The QR code linking to actual lab reports stuck — that's the one thing that separates "we test our stuff" copy from a brand that's actually showing receipts.

pain_map.pain: For the informed enthusiast (ambiguous but on-spec), self-published FSSAI-lab QR reports fail to clear the trust bar because the reference standard in their head is an INDEPENDENT seal (Informed-Choice / Labdoor); the ad's own-lab proof reads as brand-marking-its-own-homework, so the paranoid buyer the copy targets is exactly the one it can't convert on-surface.
pain_map.prevalence: recurring across enthusiast_macros_lifter in research/browse contexts

evidence_quotes.quote: No Informed-Choice or Labdoor certification visible anywhere on the pack, just their own QR to their own reports — that's the whole problem with the Indian market and this doesn't clear it.
no third-party seal I recognise anywhere on the front, just "FSSAI approved labs" which is not the same thing.
Their own QR to their own test reports is not Informed-Choice, and until I see an independent seal I'm not moving off what I already trust.

pain_map.pain: The ad opens a price/value loop it never closes on-surface: on-spec enthusiasts uniformly halt at unknown price-per-serving vs an already-benchmarked incumbent (Biozyme), converting interest into a comparison-shop that defaults back to the incumbent — the switching case is never made where the buyer is standing.

evidence_quotes.quote: I don't know the price per serving and I'm not switching off Biozyme until I run that number against my current ₹108 benchmark — that's the only gate that matters.
I don't know the price per serving versus Biozyme, and until I run that number there's nothing to decide.
this is probably more expensive per kg and unflavoured means I'm doing extra work every shake, so the switching cost isn't zero.

pain_map.pain: The 'unflavoured' spec, meant as a purity signal, functions as a usage-friction wall for the aspirant clean-label crowd: they read it as homework/commitment they can't picture executing, so even buyers whose values the copy nails stall on 'what would I actually do with this' — a comprehension-to-consideration leak among the very audience the aesthetic attracts.
pain_map.prevalence: widespread among aspirant_clean_label and some enthusiasts, browse/research contexts

evidence_quotes.quote: Unflavoured means I have to figure out what to mix it with and whether it tastes like nothing or tastes like bad nothing, and that feels like homework I haven't signed up for yet.
I'm not sure I need 1kg of something unflavoured sitting in my kitchen feeling like homework.

pain_map.pain: The product is whey, and the aspirant clean-label buyer has already made plant-based an IDENTITY filter, not a preference — so the clean-label copy that most attracts them collides with a self-image wall no in-scope lever moves; the creative's best-fit aesthetic audience is disqualified at the category level before price or proof matter.
pain_map.prevalence: dominant and consistent across aspirant_clean_label, all contexts

evidence_quotes.quote: It's whey, not plant-based — that's the wall, full stop, and no amount of clean labelling gets me over it.
It's whey, and I've been telling myself I'm plant-based for long enough that buying this would feel like a small betrayal of something.
"plant-based" isn't just a preference for me at this point, it's kind of the whole filter.

pain_map.pain: In low-attention feeds the minimal 'D2C-snack-pouch' aesthetic backfires: it fails to trip the 'this is a protein I care about' filter fast enough, so on-spec enthusiasts scroll past before the 30g/QR signals load — the design that earns trust in research contexts costs attention at the top of the funnel in commute/late-night.
pain_map.prevalence: recurring among enthusiast_macros_lifter and some clean-label in commute_scroll / late_night

pain_map.pain: For the outside-target hair/collagen switcher and the bar-eating snacker the ad is category-irrelevant, and the transparency angle they DO admire only reinforces envy for their own category — a media-buy targeting leak, not a creative failure, but it confirms the ad has no cross-category pull to widen the funnel.

evidence_quotes.quote: Whey protein for gym goals doesn't connect to anything I'm currently buying for

I keep thinking I wish the Plix collagen label was that upfront about what's not in it.

strengths_to_preserve.strength: The 'made without' list and direct naming of amino-spiking/adulteration is the ad's sharpest hook — it lands as a real mechanism, not a claim, precisely with the purity-anxious skeptic it targets.

evidence_quotes.quote: the "made without" list is longer than the "made with" list, which feels like it's directly talking to someone who's been burned by sketchy supplements before, which is basically me.
they named amino-spiking directly, which is the kind of thing only someone who knows the scam would write.

strengths_to_preserve.strength: The 'we don't want you to take our word for it' + QR-to-reports line is the one move that stops the reflexive scroll and earns cautious credibility from a category-jaded skeptic.

evidence_quotes.quote: The third-party testing callout and the QR code to actual lab reports genuinely caught me — that's the one thing that would make me pause instead of scroll, because "we don't want you to take our word for it" is exactly what every other brand *doesn't* say.
The QR code to lab reports stuck — not the product itself, but the fact that they acknowledged the adulteration thing directly instead of pretending it doesn't exist.

strengths_to_preserve.strength: The non-gym, cafe/grocery aesthetic successfully removes the bro-brand barrier and gives clean-label buyers a product they wouldn't be embarrassed to shelve — genuine differentiation from MuscleBlaze/OZiva.

evidence_quotes.quote: the packaging actually looks like something I'd see at a cafe rather than a gym counter, which is... different.
it didn't look like a protein powder I'd be embarrassed to have on my shelf.

pre_purchase_research.friction_summary: Highest engagement and trust land here, but every engaged buyer defers to an off-ad QR scan or price check, and the within-target skeptic still stalls on the no-gym-habit blocker.

weekend_afternoon_browse.friction_summary: Clean-label copy and packaging pull saves/seek-info among aspirants, but whey/plant identity and unflavoured friction cap conversion; skeptics admire but don't act.

late_night_wind_down.friction_summary: Signals register faintly but tired, low-intent scrolling flattens most reactions to 'clock it and forget'; a few enthusiasts park it for later.

commute_scroll.friction_summary: The minimal snack-pouch aesthetic fails to trip the protein filter fast enough, so even on-spec buyers scroll past before the 30g/QR proof loads.
